subject: Coordinating ML/Infra technical playbook session (60-90m) — times & attendees
messages:
From: Samantha Li <s.li@medisync.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-discovery — request for ML/infra deep technical session

Hi Jonas / Ben,

Thanks again for the call today — we appreciated the concise run-through of Redwood's architecture and serving guarantees. From our side, the engineering and security leads want a deeper technical session to validate performance, caching behavior, and data controls before we move to procurement.

High-level ask: a 60–90 minute technical playbook session (ML + Infra leads) to:
- walk through request routing and fallback behavior
- examine KV cache and prefix caching implications for our use case
- review quantization and latency trade-offs with our sequence lengths
- confirm telemetry/trace artifacts we can consume for audits

Preferred windows next week (PDT):
- Wednesday 21 Jul: 13:00–14:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Thursday 22 Jul: 09:00–10:30 or 11:00–12:30

Attendees from MediSync: myself (product), Carlos Torres (ML lead), Priya Nambiar (infra/security). Can you confirm who from Redwood should join (ML infra engineer + ops)?

I've attached the discovery notes we took and a short list of compliance questions to help you prep.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Director, Product
MediSync

Attachment: discovery-notes-20260706.pdf (document stub)

Thanks Samantha — really glad the discovery was useful. We're happy to run a focused 60–90 minute playbook session. Proposed attendees from Redwood: me (solutions), Ben Carter (technical account lead), and Grace O'Connor (serving runtime engineer). If we need a product or security SME we'll loop them in.

Of the windows you suggested, we can do:
- Wed 21 Jul 15:00–16:30 PDT (preferred)
- Thu 22 Jul 11:00–12:30 PDT (backup)

Draft agenda (60–90 min):
1) 10m — goals and success criteria (you + Redwood)
2) 25m — architecture walkthrough: routing, fallback tiers, and model pinning
3) 20m — hands-on latency/throughput examples, KV caching patterns for short/long prefixes
4) 15m — security/compliance touchpoints (data path, logs, KMS options)
5) 10–20m — open Q&A + next steps / mutual action items

Prep items for MediSync: short sequence-length distribution, expected QPS, and any eval prompts you want us to sanity-check. We'll upload a one-page prep note and a calendar invite once you lock the time.

If Wed 15:00 PDT works, I can send the invite now.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
